q: If allowed, which ceiling finish suits the nursing wards best?

q: Among these materials, which has the lowest embodied energy?

q: Per the zoning ordinance, how should this proposed facility be classified?

q: Laying out gypsum board for maximum sheet efficiency over the 93-square-meter eave area, how many boards are required?
n: A standard gypsum board sheet measures 1.22 m x 2.44 m (about 2.98 sq. m.). Dividing the 93 sq. m. eave area by this sheet size and rounding up for full-sheet coverage gives 32 pieces, per the given eave area in the source document.

n: Health centers and similar facilities serving non-ambulatory patients fall under Group D, Division D-2 of the Institutional (Government and Health Services) occupancy classification, per PD 1096 IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1, Group D, Division D-2.

q: Per BP 344, what slope is most desirable for a PWD-accessible pedestrian ramp?
n: BP 344's accessibility standards set 1:12 as the maximum allowable slope for a PWD ramp, per BP 344, IRR (Accessibility Law) — Ramp Slope Requirement.

q: Given the site's dimensions and slope, what is the total elevation difference across the grade?
n: With a 20-meter frontage on a 1,200 sq. m. lot, the site depth is 60 meters (1,200 ÷ 20). At a 4% grade, the elevation change across that depth is 60 x 0.04 = 2.40 meters, per the given site figures in the source document.
